sourceDescription: NASA-hosted OCR of the uncorrected Technical Air-to-Ground Voice Transcription (GOSS NET 1). NASA states no copyright is asserted for these raw transcripts.
limitations: One UTC calendar day, not a wake-to-sleep day. The moonwalk occurs on the following UTC date and is outside this dataset.
Only CDR labels are attributed to Armstrong. SC and MS are not assigned to him. Ground and other crew speech is retained as context.
OCR and the original transcription may contain timing, word and speaker errors. The source is uncorrected.
Recorded turns do not establish recording coverage, actual silence, task duration or response latency.
No health signals, voice acoustics, personal baseline or cognitive-overload labels accompany this transcript.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. We're standing by. Out.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, Houston. We'll be done with P22 in just a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy all that. You're looking good.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. You copy that NOUN 49 on your downlink? If you've had enough time, I'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We got it. Go ahead, Mike.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We see a NOUN 89. You can do the VERB 34 now. Over. Beat me to it.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes. I've done it, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: All that procedure for P22 seemed to work very well. The only thing that was a little odd, is that there was some DAP thruster activity. I had pitch in ACCEL COMMAND, and roll and yaw in RATE COMMAND, and somehow, roll and yaw got excited and the DAP went into a flurry of thruster firing. We've noticed the same thing in the CMS, and just written it off as a CMS peculiarity.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We saw that activity, Mike. We'll see if we can track it down and let you know. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. You can proceed to sleep attitude now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's in work, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, we're holding inertial a little while to study the approach to the landing zone.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, this is Apollo ... in the Eagle - Apollo 11 in the Eagle. I've got ... for our landing area.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. You are breaking up badly. Say again. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I can see the entire landing area from the position I'm in looking out the left window in the LM.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. Understand you can see the entire landing area looking out the LM windows. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Say again. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We got a lot of noise on the downlink. Would you please try your high gain in wide beamwidth, and the angles are 180 the yaw and pitch zero. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. How do you read us on the high gain? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Mike. You're a lot better now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. You want a wide beam for some reason?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative. We got you in the shadows, though. You are looking right down along the engine bell towards the Earth so we need you in wide beam. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. We're starting our maneuvers to sleep attitude. Roll 82, pitch 229, yaw zero.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. The angles you got in the flight plan will he good when you get there.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. We are on page activation 12 and 13, step 4, and verify descent talkbacks gray, and they're barberpole.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We would like you to take the low voltage taps OFF; RESET, then 0N. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Stand by. We got it. We just had one circuit breaker out of position.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: We have them gray now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: ... should have warmed up by now.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Oh, he's transmitting on B.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Hey, Mike, you transmitting on B?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11 - Apollo 11/Eagle. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Eagle. This is Houston. We read you. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I read you about four by four. Could you give me a short count, please?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Eagle. Coming in with the short count - 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Houston out. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Are you copying my low bit rate? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We got some beautiful data here, Eagle. We're - All those guys are looking at it - systems guys. We'll have some word for you in a minute how everything looks.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I'm all ready to switch to high bit rate if that's okay with you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Would you please stand by, Eagle. We want to get to the proper sleep attitude before we proceed on with the COMM check. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Standing by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. We'll go ahead with the camera checkout. I'm still on low taps, and I assume there's no problem doing that. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative. No problem on that, Eagle. You can go ahead and power up the sequence camera. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Should have done that before.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, be advised - sounds like a hot mike. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. If you're reading me now, I am in hot mike because I'm in ICS push to talk, snd DOWNVOICE BACKUP. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We just wanted to remind you. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Are you maneuvering to sleep attitude? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, this is Houston. We have lost all the voice and data with Columbia. Would you see if he is maneuvering to sleep attitude? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Hey, Mike. You maneuvering to sleep attitude?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I don't believe they can hear you, Mike. Are you maneuvering now to sleep attitude?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. The Columbia has maneuvered to sleep attitude. He's got the high gain antennas - antenna angles set in, and he should be communicating with you. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We don't have him. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Would you please have Columbia put in COMMAND RESET? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Wilco. COMMAND RESET.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Since we're in sleep attitude, I'll give you another long count. If you're reading in this mode, we'd like you to switch to high bit rate. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Go ahead with your short count.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. We're reading you five by. You can go to high bit rate now. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Going to high bit rate now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, this is Houston. Do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, this is Eagle. Roger. Read you loud and clear. How me? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Reading you five by also, Buzz, and we got the high bit rate. It's looking beautiful through Goldstone. Giving you a count: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Please give us a count. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger, Houston. Eagle with a count. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by. We're reading you five by. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. I'm ready to go S band voice. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by, Eagle. Stand by on step 4.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Would you please give us P00 in ACCEPT. We've got a load for you. Break. Eagle, we're ready to go to step 4. Please select S band voice to VOICE. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Eagle. This is Houston. How do you read - normal voice? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Eagle - Houston, this is Eagle. Read you loud and clear on S band, normal voice. How me? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. You're beautiful in this mode, Buzz. We're reading you five by. Coming with a short count and we'd like one back from you. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Houston out.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Houston, Eagle. You're gorgeous also. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Eagle, over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Eagle. This is better than the downvoice backup. Stand by 1

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Everybody's happy as a clam with this mode. We'd like to stay here for a little bit. Telemetry looks great, and the; voice is great. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Understand. I'm checking out camera number 4 now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Say again what you're checking out? 0ver.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger, Houston. Eagle has checked out both 70 millimeter cameras and both 16 millimeter cameras, and all work fine. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Sounds great. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We've looked over your systems on the high bit rate. Everything looks super; we're ready to go. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by. You want to go back to low bit rate now?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by on that. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We look good through the 210 on this mode. We're going to shift data select to an 85 foot dish to see what we've got, and then we'll be back to you on the 210. If you'll stand by a couple of minutes in this mode, we'll be back with you. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Eagle standing by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. How do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. Read you loud and clear. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We're reading you five by. We've got the voice good through the 85; the telemetry is in and out through the 85. Stand by. We'll be back with you through the 210. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. You can go step 5 now. We'd like low bit rate. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. You have low bit rate.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy, Eagle.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Could you give me a short count - this mode? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, this is Eagle with a short count. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Eagle. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Eagle. You're five by. This S band voice is really beautiful. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And, Eagle, Houston. We'll be standing by in this mode for a minute or so. We'll be back with you if you'll just stand by. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, this is Houston coming through the 210. How do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Read you loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, this is Houston. We're happy with all our data in all modes. You can power down the COMM now. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I understand. Eagle will power down the COMM, and we are just approaching 27 volts now. It looks like we won't have to bother with the high taps.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: We're powering down. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, this is Houston. We got a TEI 11 PAD for you and an update on the water dump. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Stand by one, Houston. Are you through with the DSKY?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. Ready to copy TEI 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Columbia. Here we come with the TEI 11. SPS G&N: 37200, minus 060, plus 047. NOUN 33, 098 05 2422, plus 41448, plus 03719, minus 02422. Roll is NA, pitch 020, the rest of the PAD is NA. Set stars are NA. The ullage is two quads - correction, two jets for 16 seconds; use Bravo and Delta. In the comments, the undocked present CSM - correction, this is for - TEI 11 is undocked. Present onboard weight of the CSM is 37200 pounds, about 50 Alfa on your DAP. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: All right. I read back: TEI 11, SPS G&N: 37200, minus 060, plus 047, plus 098, 05 2422, plus 41448, plus 03719, minus 02422; NA, 020; the rest of the PAD NA. Ullage, two jets for 16 seconds, Quads B and D. Undocked present CSM weight is okay in the DAP.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. And we'd like you to do a waste water dump at 84 hours down to 25 percent. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. I understand. Waste water dump to 25 percent at 84 hours.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And, Mike, we'll have LOS in about 11 minutes at 83 44. A0S is 84 30, and prior to - or at LOS, we would like you to go - Configure the S band for high gain track to REACQ, high gain beam to NARROW, and let's try that to see if we can get an automatic REACQ at the next AOS. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Good idea.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I'm in REACQ and NARROW now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Also, that water that you got on the aft bulkhead, we - If it's not too much, we just recommend sopping it up and then throwing the sponges away in the waste stowage area. If it's too much, then we recommend using the procedure in the checklist on page F10-14. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Would you have Buzz make sure he gives us the OPS pressure readings before you close up? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, 11. The OPS read 5750, both bottles.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Roger. Reading you fine, and it looks like the automatic REACQ went very well just as soon as you came around the limb. We have several small items to discuss with you here just before you go to sleep. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay, 11. First of all, on our LM systems checks, everything went fine. I would like to remind you, though, tomorrow you may see an ascent pressure light when you activate the MC&W. There should be no problem, however. You did note that the APS AUX tank pressure was only reading 111 psi, which is normal at this point, but below the level which will trigger your light due to the helium which has been dissolved into the propellant. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Understand that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And next item, the supercritical helium rise rate is nominal, and you also had that question for us about your thruster activity during the P22 on the last REV. Believe we understand that now, as you reported that your pitch was in ACCEL COMMAND and your yaw and roll were in RATE COMMAND. You were firing your pitch thrusters. This will couple rates into your yaw and roll axes, and the - You were at that time holding only half a degree deadband and coupling rates into yaw and roll produced the extra firings about the yaw and roll axes. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes. That may be true. It's very peculiar coupling, in that it waits longer than you would think and its reaction is greater than you would think. We were getting yaw rates of around four tenths of a degree per second, for example.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Mike. We did play the data back, and that's the way it looked upon analysis of the chart recordings back here. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: They've also looked at the results of your landmark tracking. The marks all apparently were very good, and we've got a full page of data here relative to the altitudes of the various site locations, which I won't read up to you, but I did want to let you know that the marks apparently went very well. I also have your consumable budgets, particularly your RCS propellant quantities. They're Deltas from nominal if you should want them. Your worst quad is quad Charlie, which is 9 percent low. I'll not read up the others unless you want them. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. How about the O2 fuel cell purge? You want that now?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: I'll have to stand by just a moment.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. And then the other one is, we're still charging battery A.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We would like to delay the fuel cell purge until the backside of the Moon, and you go ahead and - should terminate your battery charge at this time. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Understand. I knew we had another O2 and H2 purge coming up in the morning; I wasn't sure whether you wanted to go through with this one or not. I'll wait until the next side and then do it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's fine, Buzz.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Terminate battery charging now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's right, and one other systems item here - in order to balance your CRYO tanks, would you get your O2 tank 1 and your H 2 tank 2 heaters off? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. I have O2 tank heater 1 off, and H2 tank heater 2 off.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's right, Mike, and we believe you have your quad Bravo and quad Charlie turned off in your DAP at this time, and a 5 degree deadband. We'd prefer a 10 degree deadband for your sleep period overnight here. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: One other item relative to a malfunction procedure. It's unlikely that you'll have to worry about this tomorrow, but in your malfunction list under docking on page F11 9, there is a malfunction procedure for a high O2 flow rate at the top of - under tunnel at the top of page 11 9. We would like to have you not use that malfunction procedure should you encounter the high O2 flow rate, and instead, check back with Houston for a revised procedure should you find that situation. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Understand, and note has been made in my checklist.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Roger. That just about takes care of all the items we have here on the ground before time to hit the sack, and I guess you will have a presleep check for us before you go to bed.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. We're in the midst of cycling the O2 and H2 fans now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And the radiation is as follows: CDR 11012, CMP 100l3, LMP 09015. Negative medication. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy, 11.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. We're thinking about taking the monocular with us on into the LM. We think it might prove to be of some use. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. It sounds like a good idea for some of your surveying work there inside the cockpit. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. You want to run that by with whoever might be concerned?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: I sure will.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We have apparently lost the high gain lock. We would appreciate it if you would give us a help manually to try to relock up on the high gain. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. ..

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Reading you very weak, still too far down in the noise to complete the full transmission. If you'd give us a hand on a manual relock, we'd appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We're still unable to pick you up on the high gain antenna. Request you go to MANUAL, and wide beamwidth. The pitch and yaw angles in your checklist are good ones. You should be able to find us there. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. How do you read now?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Loud and clear this time. How me?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Loud and clear. You faded out on your last transmission. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Are you in wide beam now?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Negative. I got you locked back on again REACQ and narrow.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. That's all we want. We want to stay in narrow, and we're a little puzzled about why we lost you here a few minutes ago. Do you have any ideas?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: No, we sure don't (cough) - sure don't. We're showing - we're showing about 15 degrees plus pitch and about 270. That ought to be good and clear.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We concur there. We still don't have any good ideas on why we were lost then.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Would you confirm that we did acquire automatically when you came around the limb for this passage. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: That's confirmed.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. On your AUTO RCS SELECT switches, we show quad Bravo disabled but quad Charlie only partially disabled. Charlie 3, I believe, is the only one you have selected off. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes. Roger. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: How do they look to you now, Houston?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We see them all disabled at this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We're going to try to check out this ability to automatically reacquire on the S band, and what we want to do is to secure our uplink carrier for about 30 seconds. Then we will turn it back on and see if the spacecraft equipment will automatically reacquire. So if you do not get a call from us within about 3 minutes, that means we have not been able to reacquire and request your assistance on a manual acquisition. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. We understand.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We also would appreciate - if you will note the angles that the antenna tracks through in its attempt to reacquire. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. It looks like we're locked back up again with no delay. How does it look on board? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. The signal strength dropped very rapidly to zero; and the pitch and yaw, in about 3 secconds, moved toward 40 degrees pitch and 240 degrees yaw. Right now, they're sitting on about 15 degrees pitch and about 265 degrees yaw. So they didn't move very far, about 30 degrees apiece; and then they picked right back on up again. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Some of "The Luckiest People" in the background there. We copied your pitch and yaw angles.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Could you give us the location of your - pitch and yaw location of your position indicators? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. They're in the same position as the antenna right now; plus 15 degrees pitch and - no, now wait a minute. I got them - got it at about 275 instead of 265.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We'd like to try the same procedure once more. We'll leave the carrier a little longer and be back up for a call within 4 minutes. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We're locked back up again. Can you give us a report on how the antenna behaved?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. It was essentially identical as before. The pitch went to 45, 40 to 45 and the yaw went to about - to about 255, 245 to 255; and then it rather quickly locked up at 15 degrees pitch and 270 yaw. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Roger. Your angles are 45 and 255. Do I understand that as soon as the carrier dropped, it went to these angles; or did it only go to these angles after the uplink carrier was reenabled and the antenna began to reacquire? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: No. As soon as the carrier dropped off, why, it drifted over into those angles and stayed there. Then when it came back up again, why, it hunted around for a while, but it didn't get any further off. Gradually brought it on in to the angles where it is right now; and then the signal strength would take several jumps as evidently it goes from wide to medium to narrow. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Understand. And on another subject, request you zero your optics for the night. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Zeroed.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Can you confirm that you have changed the CO2 filter as per flight plan in the last hour? Over?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: No. We're still eating. We're about to do it. We'll let you know.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. And we've got about 14 minutes until LOS. A0S is 86 30, an hour away. We're wondering whether or not you plan to have one man up at that time or would you all like to be asleep inside the next hour? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Somebody will be up.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. The thing that we're still puzzling on is the antenna, and if - as long as there will be somebody up, why, we would like to have somebody check the automatic REACQ on the next AOS.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. We'll do that. We haven't chlorinated the water yet, and we haven't changed the lithium hydroxide. We're just still finishing up dinner.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Mike. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We have LOS coming up in 2 minutes now, and A0S will be at 86 plus 28 plus 15. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: We'll see you on the other side, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Loud and clear here. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. We just appeared to get a solid lock for the last - oh, about a minute. The ... needle's been wandering up and down, and the pitch and yaw needles have been wandering around, but it appears to have reacquired by itself solidly now. We're just finishing up our fuel cell purge. Hydrogen on number 3 is the last to go off. It'll be coming off in just a second.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We believe we've tracked down the reacquisition problem we had on the previous REV. It looks like it was a receiver power supply here on the ground and no problems in the spacecraft at all. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Glad to hear it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, that really winds things up as far as we're concerned on the ground, for the evening. We're ready to go to bed and get a little sleep. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes. We're about to join you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Apollo 11. Good morning from the Black Team.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Good morning, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Good morning. We got about 2 minutes to LOS here, Mike.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: ... You guys wake up early.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: (Laughing) Yes, you're about 2 minutes early on the wakeup. Looks like you were really sawing them away.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. For planning purposes, you can go ahead and take the monocular into the LM with you.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. I'll tell them. How are all the CSM systems looking?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Looks like the command module's in good shape. Black Team has been watching it real closely for you.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: We sure appreciate that. Because I sure haven't.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I say because I sure have not.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11. Thirty seconds. AOS will be 94 plus 21.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Standing by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Go.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. How do you read the BIOMED in the LMP with the LCG on? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by, 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We have good data on all 3 crewmen. No. Belay that. The Commander we do not have yet.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. He's not up yet.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. We just had a very good view of the landing site. We can pick out almost all of the features we've identified previously.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Roger. Sounds real fine. And, 11, I have your maneuver PAD and consumables update whenever you want them.

utterances.speaker: SC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Stand by a little, please.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We're standing by. And that's the block data on the maneuver PAD, by the way.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11 is a couple of minutes away from this rolling right 40 degrees to roll 122, pitch 229, yaw 0. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Roger. We're standing by.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Apollo 11, Houston. Here's your block data, TEI 30. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: SPS/G&N: 36639; your NOUN 48, minus 072, plus 051; your NOUN 33, 135 24 4000; NOUN 81, plus 32178, plus 06036, minus 01304, your pitch 064. The rest is NA. Ullage: two jet, 16 seconds; and it's based on L0I REFSMMAT. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. TEI 30 SPS/G&N: 36639 minus 072, plus 051, 135 24 4000, plus 32178, plus 06036, minus 01304, pitch 064, two jets 16 second, LOI REFSMMAT. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Readback correct. Your consumables update?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. GET 91 plus 30, minus 7 percent; Alfa minus 8, Bravo minus 2.5, Charlie minus 10, Delta minus 6.5. H2 total, minus 2 pounds; oxygen total, plus 9 pounds. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And on board, we're reading for quad Alfa 75 percent, Bravo 78, Charlie 78, and Delta 77 percent.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. I have your base line altitude update now, if Buzz is ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Alfa 1 is 500, that's 500 feet above the landing site. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Alfa 1 is 500 feet above the landing site. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Our crew status report for sleep: CDR 5.5, CMP 6.0, LMP 5.0. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Roger. We have that now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. The "Black Bugle" just arrived with some morning news briefs if you're ready.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Church services around the world today are mentioning Apollo 11 in their prayers. President Nixon's worship service at the White House is also dedicated to the mission, and our fellow astronaut, Frank Borman, is still in there pitching and will read the passage from Genesis which was read on Apollo 8 last Christmas. The Cabinet and members of Congress, with emphasis on the Senate and House space committees, have been invited, along with a number of other guests. Buzz, your son, Andy, got a tour of MSC yesterday. Your Uncle Bob Moon accompanied him on the visit which included the LRL. Among the - -

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: - - Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Among the large headlines concerning Apollo this morning, there's one asking that you watch for a lovely girl with a big rabbit. An ancient legend says a beautiful Chinese girl called Chang-o has been living there for 4000 years. It seems she was banished to the Moon because she stole the pill of immortality from her husband. You might also look for her companion, a large Chinese rabbit, who is easy to spot since he is always standing on his hind feet in the shade of a cinnamon tree. The name of the rabbit is not reported.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. We'll keep a close eye out for the bunny girl.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. You residents of the spacecraft Columbia may be interested in knowing that today is Independence Day in the country of Colombia. Gloria Diaz of the Philippines was crowned Miss Universe last night. She defeated 60 other girls for the global beauty title. Miss Diaz is 18, with black hair and eyes, and measures 34-1/2, 23, 34-1/2. First runner up was Miss Australia, followed by Miss Israel, and Miss Japan. While you're on your way back Tuesday night, the American and National League Allstars will be playing ball in Washington. Mel Stottlemyre of the Yankees is expected to be the American League's first pitcher. No one is predicting who will be first pitcher for the National League yet. They have nine on the roster. Even though research has certainly paid off in the space program, research doesn't always pay off, it seems. The Woodstream Corporation, parent company of the Animal Trap Company of America which has made more than a billion wooden spring mousetraps, reports that it built a better mousetrap but the world didn't beat a door to its path - didn't beat a path to its door. As a matter of fact, the company had to go back to the oldfashioned kind. They said, "We should have spent more time researching housewives and less time researching mice". And the "Black Beag - Bugle" is all completed for the morning.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We appreciate the news.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Black Team, we'll be looking for an interesting day with you all tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We'll be going off here shortly, and we'll pick you up in the morning for sure.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Three minutes to LOS; AOS at 96 plus 20.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Apollo 11. 96 20. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Columbia. Houston. Do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Hello, Houston, this is Eagle. How do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, this is Houston. Are you calling? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. How do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Reading you about three by, Buzz; a lot of noise on the loop. We think it's coming from Columbia, but we can't tell. We're unable to raise voice with him. Would he please go to high gain. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. I'll have him go to high gain. It's probably the glycol pump you hear in the background, and I'm up to the point where I turn on the IMU. Would you recommend I hold off here for a few minutes or go ahead and power up the IMU? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Hey, get your high gain to working.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, this is Houston. You can turn on the IMU. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, this is Columbia.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston ...

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Eagle. This is Houston. We've got a noisy downlink on the downvoice backup. Would you please select S band voice to VOICE? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. Reading you loud and clear. How me?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. About three by, Mike. We've got a lot of noise in the background. It's clearing up now. Break. Eagle, Houston. Do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. About four by four. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Just getting a voice check. Say the page you're on in the activation checklist. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I'm on page 27. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Understand 27. We copy. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Would you please give us P00 in ACCEPT. We have a state vector for you. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Stand by one.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. You have P00 in ACCEPT, and how are you reading me now?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Understand, we have P00 in ACCEPT. You're about three by in - on the voice, Mike. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. You're coming in loud and clear, and I'm configured for normal voice. If you've got any switch changes, let me know.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We've got some noise somewhere in the system down here, I think. We're working on it. And I've got a 130 landmark update for you, and also a DAP load whenever you're ready to copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Stand by one.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead with the 130 update.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Mike. Coming at you with the 130, P1 is 98 37 35, P2 98 42 44, 4 miles north. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. P1 98 37 35, P2 98 42 44, 4 miles north of track; and go ahead with your DAP load.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. CSM weight 36651, LM weight 33627, pitch trim minus 0.72, yaw trim plus 0.51. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Both are good readbacks. Out.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. Are you satisfied with the LGC self test? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Understand. You passed the LGC self test. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Negative. I was asking you if you were satisfied with it. As far as I can tell, it's satisfactory. And also the primary EVAP flow is actuated to number 1 at 96 05. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy on the primary EVAP. We've got the low bit rate, Buzz. We couldn't see that LGC self test. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. The docking tunnel index angle remains unchanged.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy. Out.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle is going to secondary transmitter/receiver and secondary power amplifier, and I'll check with you in 60 seconds. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by. We're standing by. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We are through with the computer. You can go back to BLOCK. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. On secondary transmitter/receiver and power amplifier, how do you read? Over. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Reading you five by, Buzz. How me? 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Out.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. That's about the same as before. Switching back to PRIMARY.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. Back on PRIMARY, and I'm ready to proceed with the steerable antenna activation.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We're standing by, Buzz. Go ahead. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And I'll go to BIOMED left - right momentarily.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. Got a real nice lock on - lockon on the steerable antenna, and you should be receiving BIOMED right and PCM high. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Eagle. We got you five by. It's really beautiful. We've got the high bit rate and the BIOMED. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Do you copy? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Copy.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. For your information, we're doing the glycol pump check now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And there's the secondary glycol pump.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And I'm on secondary, or number 2 pump right now, and I'll hold here for a couple of seconds and then switch back to number 1.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Columbia. We noticed your DAP configuration. We'd like you to turn off B3 and C4, Mike, and for register 2 in the DAP, we'd like all ones. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: B3 and C4 are both off on panel 8 and I understand you want - Say again what you want on register 2.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. In the DAP, we'd like you load all ones. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Did you hit the COMMAND RESET around - after LOS on the last pass? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's affirmative. When we were having difficulty getting you, Charlie, I pushed the COMMAND RESET to make sure I had control of high gain.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you much. We're in good shape now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. Can you tell me if you're picking up BIOMED on the CDR now? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We're not getting any BIOMED from the CDR now. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Understand.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We got the BIOMED on the commander now. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. We're ready for an E memory dump if you are. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We're ready. Go.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, this is Houston. We see the optics zero switch on. Before you take some marks, don't forget to cycle it back off and on, and then on. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Houston, Eagle here. I wish we had one of those optics. I'll tell Mike about it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Columbia. Excuse me. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Could you give us a hack on the time that you switched to LM power and also verify that we're on glycol pump 1. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: This is Eagle. We're on pump 1, stand by for the switchover time.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: The switch time to LM power is 95 54 00. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy, Neil. Is Buzz back in the Columbia now? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Yes. He is.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Hello, Columbia, this is Eagle on Simplex B. How do you read?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You are loud and clear in Simplex B, Neil.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Read you loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Would you configure for Simplex A, please?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Going to Simplex A.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Columbia, Eagle. How do you read on VHF A?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Reading you loud and clear on A.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Read you loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: And I'm ready to get a time hack from you. Load the CSM time.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Do you want the T EPHEM first?

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Let's get your clock first and then we'll get T EPHEM.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Give me a time for load.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: 97 01 30. Correction on that, Neil. 97 - make that 97 03 30.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. I have 97 03 30 set in.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. And you've got about a minute to go.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: 15 seconds to go. 10. 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: MARK it.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Let's do a 0665 on my Mark.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Did you get that, Mike?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Standing by for your Mark.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: MARK.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. I'm within three hundredths. That's within our ability to keep together, I think.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Now you want to give me T EPHEM VERB 05, NOUN 01 ENTER?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. I've got VERB 05, NOUN 01, ENTER. Going to 17 06 ENTER.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Are you ready to copy?

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Register 1, 5 balls; register 2, 20017; register 3, 20616. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Understand R1, 5 zeros; R2, 20017; R3, 20616.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: And I'm standing by configured to record your PCM data.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: And I'm ready to start on a docked IMU coarse align when you are; and when you're ready, go MIN deadband ATT hold.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: We're minimum deadband, attitude hold.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Now I need your NOUN 20.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. I got VERB 06, NOUN 20. Give me a Mark on it.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: MARK.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Register 1, plus 11202, plus 20741, plus 00211. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. That coarse align looked good to us. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay, Mike. Your attitude hold's no longer required.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay, Mike. I'd like to copy a NOUN 20 again, 06 NOUN 20. Be on my Mark.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Standing by for your Mark.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: 3, 2, 1; stand by. Take it again.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: MARK.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, I read plus 11154, plus 20792, plus 00230. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. I -

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay, Houston. Did you copy -

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We have the angles. I'll read them back. Over. For the command module, 11154, 20792, 00230. For the LM, 18995, 02852, 35863. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: That's correct for Eagle and command module.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Did you get the time? Was 97 14 20.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy, Eagle. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia and Eagle: LOS for both spacecrafts 97 32, AOS 98 18. Houston, out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle,Houston. We have your gyro torquing angles if you're ready to copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. We're ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Eagle. For X minus 00060, Y plus 00620, Z plus 01080. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Understand. X minus 00060, Y plus 00620, Z plus 01080.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Eagle. Good readback. Out.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, this is Eagle. Do you want us to go ahead and do a VERB 42 at this time?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by. That's affirmative, Eagle. We'd like you to go ahead and fine align. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle, LMP. How do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Five by, Buzz. How me? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Loud and clear. I'm going to be going through an ascent battery check. You want to check my BIOMED's briefly? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We got a good BIOMED on you, Buzz. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Let me know where it ought to be at this point.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. You can stay there at that point. When we go LOS, we'd like you to go off on the BIOMED. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Do you copy those angles, Houston - torquing angles?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. They're correct. You can torque. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We have about 4 minutes LOS. That makes A0S 98 18. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Eagle. Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Columbia. Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Eagle, Columbia.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Columbia, Eagle. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. The capture latch is in the probe or engaged in the drogue. Would you like to set them from your side?

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. ED battery A is 37.0 and battery B is 36.9. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy both of those, Buzz. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We looked at the E memory. It's GO. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. E memory GO.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Mike, the capture latches look good.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We'd like you to go to the OMNI antenna, and next AOS, we'd like you to be in forward. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Going to - which 0MNI do you want now, aft?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We'd like aft now and forward at AOS. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Thirty seconds to LOS. Both spacecraft looking good going over the hill. Out.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Better keep it pretty close to your mouth, though.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We're standing by. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. No voice. Will you verify forward OMNI? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We have no voice with Eagle. Would you please verify that Eagle is on forward 0MNI. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Are you reading me, Buzz? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I've got you now. I fed in those angles for the S band but I couldn't get a lockon because the antenna would be looking through the LM in order to reach the Earth. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copied in the P22 attitude that you will not be able to get a high gain lockon. We have a DAP data load, if you're ready to copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. LM weight 33627, CSM weight 36651, pitch trim 00470, roll trim 00589. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. LM weight 33627, CSM weight 36651, pitch trim 00470, roll trim 00589. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. That's a good readback. You're about two by with these OMNI's in this configuration; we won't have very good COMM until we get through with the P22. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Understand.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Would you select S band voice to VOICE. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. Downvoice backup. Do you read?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We read you. Columbia, did you call? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Affirmative. Downvoice backup. How do you read me?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Better, Mike. We're reading you now about four by. No voice at all with you earlier. Let's stay in this configuration. Eagle, are you in VOICE mode? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Eagle is in VOICE mode. How do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. You're about three by now, Buzz. We're satisfied with this COMM configuration. Let's stay with where we are. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia is in OMNI Charlie downvoice backup, and if you get a chance, would you look up the coordinates of 130 for me, please? I have been - conflicting information between my cue card and my flight plan. I'd like to know which coordinate values you want me to use.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. Completed gear extension okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We're satisfied with what you already have loaded in P22 for these coordinates. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. The coordinates you have loaded in P22 are - we have - are Site 130 prime. Do you concur? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I have the coordinates loaded on the cue card which are for crater 130.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We made an error on those coordinates. We'd like you to load for latitude in a NOUN 89 plus 01 243, longitude over 2 plus 11 844, altitude minus 001 46 as shown in the flight plan. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: To Columbia?

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: He says he'll do that as soon as he gets around there.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Could you give us an idea where you are in the activation? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. We're just sitting around waiting for something to do. We need a state vector, a REFSMMAT, a reading on the AGS. And we need you to watch our DAP load, give a voice check, and throttle check. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Eagle, we'll have the state vectors and the REFSMMAT as soon as we get the high gain. Over. It will be about another 10 minutes or so before we get throug the P22, and when we maneuver to attitude and get the high gain, we'll have the updates for you. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. We'll go ahead with the DAP and throttle ... check if you don't have the gimble drive check, okay?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Understand you're going to the DAP throttle check. That's affirmative.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. These T1 and T2 times are still good, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I say the T1 and T2 times remain unchanged, don't they?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, Eagle. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. In the first of - on page 47, step 1, we had the guidance control in PGNS and mode control PGNS AUTO and, of course, the circuit breakers are not in on the thrusters yet. So when we started through the DAP and proceeded on NOUN 46 - and we're looking at NOUN 47 now, so we've got an RCS TTA light and we've got four out of the eight other bright colored red flags. I think that this is explained by the fact that we are in PGNS and AUTO and unable to fire the thrusters.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. You are correct. The lights are there and the flags because we haven't closed the breakers yet. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: And Houston, Eagle. Are you going to use the high gain before you can look at our GDA position indicator?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We can see all the throttle data - -

utterances.speaker: MS
utterances.text: I can give high ...

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead. Over. 0k 02 40 43 CDR I could give you high bit rate on the OMNI if that would help any.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Negative. We have all the throttle data we need. You can stay low bit rate. You can proceed through the throttle test, but do not do the gimbal trim. Over. Repeat, do not do the gimbal trim.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Understand.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Boy, you just can't miss those check points, Diamondback and Sidewinder.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: AUTO optics are pointed just a little bit north of crater 130.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy, Columbia, Out.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. We are ready to pressurize the RCS. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. You can go ahead with your RCS pressurizaLion, but we would like to hold off on RCS checkout until we get the high bit rate. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And Eagle, Houston. Have you deployed the landing gear yet? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: That's affirmative. The landing gear is out and ...

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. I've completed my marks. I've gone ACCEL COMMAND in all three axes to prevent that thruster firing that last time.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. Say again on the necessary data on the downlink. Let me know and I'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, stand by on the NOUN 49. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Standing by, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We got your NOUN 49; you can proceed. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Colum - correction, Eagle, Houston. We see the MASTER ARM, you can go ahead and press. We see the press now. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Looks good.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. If you've got - would like, I've got your AGS abort constants. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. For your AGS address 224, plus 60267; 225, plus 58148; 226, plus 70312; 227, minus 50031. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Good readback. Out.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Eagle, Columbia. My P22 is complete. I'm continuing this maneuver to AGS CAL attitude.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Fine. We copy.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Columbia. Your high gain angles are - Corrected - Eagle, Houston. Your high gain angles are 165 pitch, yaw 66. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. ...

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Stand by about another ...

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. I think I've got you on the high gain antenna now. AGS are go.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. If you go to REACQ on the high gain, we can acquire you now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We got some loads for you if you'll give us P00 and DATA. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: You've got P00 and DATA.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We've got both of you on the high gains now. It sounds great now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Copy. Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. I have a SEP PAD if you're ready to copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Stand by one.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Mike. SEP PAD, RCS/G&N: NOUN 47 and NOUN 48 are NA, NOUN 33, 100 395 000, N0UN 81 is NA, roll 000 007 000. Rest of PAD is NA.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: SEP, RCS/G&N at a TIG of 100 39 50: roll 0, pitch 007, yaw 0. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Good readback.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. Are you ready for us to start the RCS checkout now?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: As soon as we finish the uplink. Stand by one. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. Comment on P22. Worked just fine. The crater I marked on is a small crater down inside crater 130 as described by John Young.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. On our load - during our load, we had to do a VERB 96 to stop integration. We're going to start over again on this load. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Eagle. Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And, Eagle, here. I have read out address in the AGS 404, 405 and 406, and I had believed that 405 and 406 would both be all zeros, and I would propose maybe that I reset them to zero. I realize that 404 should be a negative number, and it is minus 13495. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Housten. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Buzz, we've got - The only thing we're missing here is the drift check. After we finish our load, we'd like you to do the drift check with Columbia. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: GO.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. The 404, 405, 406 look fine to us. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I am going to be setting them up to zero for the undocking. The question is do you want me to reset 404, 405, 406 back to the numbers that they are now, or can I leave them zero? I intend to set 404 to a minus 13495. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We would like you to zero, as called out in the timeline, all three addresses, 404, 405, 406, before undocking. After docking you can load them hack to the values that you have right now. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Eagle. Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And, Houston, Eagle here. Both RCS helium pressures are reading 2900. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Copy. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. There seems to be some confusion here on 405 and 406. We'd like you to zero them out prior to undocking, and after undocking you can - we'd like them still zeroed. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I agree with that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We've got the load in the - We have reselected P00; your integration is going again for you; the computer is yours. We'd like to do the drift check now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. In work.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Columbia, let's flick it in 0620 when you are ready.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Standing by until your Mark, Neil.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: MARK.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We've copied the angles and will read back if you are ready. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Neil.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: For the CM - for Columbia: 35864, 02073, 35954.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: That's correct, and GET was 99 hours and 4 minutes even.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. Have you initialized the AGS yet? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Negative. I haven't had a state vector yet.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. Have you done the 377 yet?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Standing by for your K factor.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We have got a load for you. Could we have P00 and ACCEPT? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You got it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you, Mike. And break. Eagle, we've got a K factor for you. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. K factor coming at you: 90 00 00 15. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. That's good. That's a good ENTER there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We recommend the AGS initial - Well, we see it coming up now on the AGS initialization. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. After the AGS initialization, we'll be ready for the RCS checkout.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We got the load in. You can go back to BLOCK.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Did you get a - copy any LM data, low bit rate, behind the Moon? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's affirmative.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Or at least I've configured for it. I'm not sure Eagle sent it or not.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: No, we did not send V data. Eagle. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. The alignment and the initialization looked good to us. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. LOS is 99 30; next AOS 100 16. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: 100 16. Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Eagle, Columbia. Let me know when you come to your RCS hot fire checks so I can disable my roll.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Wilco.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. We're right there now. And we'd like you - CSM in MID deadband ATT hold. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's where I am.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And, Houston, you have high bit rate with us now, I believe? We're ready to proceed with the RCS checks.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Eagle. We're standing by. We're ready. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Columbia, we'd like wide deadband ATT hold. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Going wide deadband ATT hold.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You got it.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Are you going to do your hot fire now?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. I'm disabling my roll.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roll is disabled.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Would you believe you've got thrusters on board that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Give me a call just as soon as your hot fire is complete, please.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Wilco.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Eagle. The RCS hot fire is complete. How did you observe it? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by. Eagle, Houston. The RCS hot fire looks super to us. We're all GO.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Mike, would you confirm that thrusters B3 and C4 are off? Over. And your radar transponder off.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: C4 is off; B3 is off. Transponder is to HEATER which is the same as being off, and I've got my roll jets back on now.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: And you're maneuvering. Right?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Will be shortly, Neil.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We're GO for undocking. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Understand.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Starting a trim maneuver to AGS CAL attitude.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, Columbia. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. There will be no television of the undocking. I have all available windows either full of heads or cameras, and I'm busy with other things.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We concur. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And, Eagle, Houston. We'd like you te select aft OMNI now. It will be good for both LOS and AOS. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Going to aft OMNI.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. One minute to LOS.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Columbia. Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: ... Columbia. Systems looking good.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Eagle. Houston. We're standing by. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We see you on the steerable. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Eagle is undocked.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. How does it look, Neil?

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: The Eagle has wings.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Looking good.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Neil. We got a - If you will give us P00 and DATA, we've got the loads for you.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. You've got it. P00 and DATA.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Let us know when you are ready to copy. We have a DOI PAD, and a PDI PAD. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR

utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: I think you've got a fine looking flying machine there, Eagle, despite the fact you're upside down.

utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: CMP

utterances.speaker: CMP

utterances.speaker: CMP

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Eagle, Columbia. I am reading you loud and scratchy. Neil is not coming through too well on his VOX. Could you be quiet for 15 seconds while I get this locked on.

utterances.speaker: CMP

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Eagle, Houston. We've got a state vector for you. We'd like P00 and DATA. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: You have it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We have a CSM rescue PAD if you are ready to copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.text: Did you copy the star - I mean the Sun check, Charlie?

utterances.text: Our radar checks indicate 50,000 foot perilune. Our visual altitude checks steadying out at about 53,000.

utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: Roger. Pitch 212, yaw plus 37.

utterances.text: Okay. Stand by.
