utterances.text: Could that, by any chance, be due to the fact that I flashed the updata link switch to DATA while that was going on? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Tranquility Base. Houston. The SPAN guys think that's conceivable. Stand by. I think we want another VERB 74.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Standing by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Tranquility Base. Houston. We'd like another VERB 74. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Here it comes.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. On my Mark it will be GET 103 53.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: MARK.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 103 53 - correction, 54.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Tranquility. Houston. We have the LM ascent PAD. If'you're ready to go. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Ready to copy the LM ascent PAD.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Tranquility. TIG, 104 39 47 00, 55358 00322, plus 0022. DEDA 47, plus 37130, minus 70615, plus 58620, plus 56936. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. LM ascent PAD: 104 39 47 00, 55358 00322, plus 0022, plus 37130, minus 70615, plus 58620, plus 56936. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Tranquility. Good readback. We also have a CSI PAD if you are ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. We are ready to go.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Coming at you with a CSI: NOUN 11, 105 35 3700, 107 11 3000, 0538, minus all zeros. FDAI is NA, 0937 - correction, 09356, 10315, plus 0538, minus all zeros, plus 0012. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Say again R1 and NOUN 86.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. R1 is plus 0538, and we have a load for you. Will you please give us P00 and DATA? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Before I do that I would like to designate the rendezvous radar up to plus-X.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. CSI readback: NOUN 11, 105 35 3700, 107 11 3000, 0538, minus all zeros, NA, 09356, 10315. NOUN 86, plus 0538, plus all zeros, and the last one was 0012. And what's the sign of that, please?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, Houston. The DELTA-VY is minus all zeros. The DELTA-VZ is plus 0012. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Plus 0012.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Good readback.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, Tranquility Base. The DSKY's yours, and updata link to DATA.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you, Tranquility.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Tranquility Base. Houston. On my Mark it will be 37 minutes to T3. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: MARK.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Thirty seven minutes till T3.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, this is Houston. It's your computer. We got the load in. You can start your P57.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Tranquility Base. Does somebody down there have a mike button keyed? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by, and we'll check.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, Houston. Do you still hear it now? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I still hear it. it sounds like somebody banging chairs around in the back room.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. That's a VOGAA that you hear for the CSM to keep the noise down on the loop. Maybe we got a MSFN relay or something. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, Houston. We got the MSFN relay in. You're hearing the VOGAA, which is a noise suppression device. We'll try to take it out. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, Houston. It ought to be a little quieter up there now. We disabled the MSFN relay.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. I think the noise has stopped now. Thank you, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. On my Mark, 25 minutes till T3. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: MARK.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Twenty five minutes until T3.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. How's it going?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We're reading you about three by. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. I'm on OMNI Charlie. How's it going?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Understand. 0MNI Charlie. Mike, be advised we have an update for you on the P22 for the LM. We estimate he landed about 4 miles downrange. Your T1 times are updated and your T2, if you're ready to copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Roger, Columbia. T1 104 32 24, 104 37 33, 2 miles south. Time of closest approach is 104 39 08.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Tranquility Base. Houston. We copy the NOUN 93. You can torque them. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You said 4 miles long, is that correct, Houston?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative, Columbia. It's about 4 miles long. Stand by. We'll have you a map location momentarily. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, Tranquility Base. Do you have an updated LM weight for us? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative. Stand by on the DAP. Our DAP PAD for you is LM weight 10906. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. 10906.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. With a latitude/longitude over two update for LM position. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Mike. We got an update on the LAT longitude for the LM, if you're ready to copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Columbia, it's plus 7 - correction, plus 0.799 for the LAT, plus 11.730 for the longitude over two. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you. The altitude remain unchanged?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Does the altitude remain unchanged? ...

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Tranquility Base. Houston. You are stay for a T3. We have some surface block data if you're ready to copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Understand we're stay for T3. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay, Houston. Go ahead with your block data.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Tranquility. Stand by one.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, Houston. Say again your T4 copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Correction on T4: 106 38 02. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Columbia. Houston. We will not come up on the MSFN relay. We'd like you to come on panel 9, turn on your VHF to TR. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. I'm on panel 9. Ready to receive. You want me to transmit for some reason with it?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again, Mike. You're about two by.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Panel 9 is configured VHF, RECEIVE. You want me to transmit with the HF for some reason? Why do you want me in TR?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, this is Houston. We don't want you to transmit, Mike. We just want you in that position in case you want to talk to Tranquility. Break. Tranquility, Houston. Say again. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. I have a fairly good sized difference between battery volts on 5 and 6; 6 is reading 33.5 and 5 is reading 36.5. Is that what you expect? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, Houston. They are both coming up in voltage. No problem. We're still GO. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Tranquility Base. Houston. Could you please give us a readout now of all of your descent tank pressures? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay, Houston. On descent 1, fuel and oxidizer are reading 10 psi; and descent 2, fuel is reading 10 psi, oxidizer 11 psi.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Tranquility. Thank you much. Out.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, Tranquility Base is ready to go through the powerdown and terminate the simulated countdown.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Standby.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Tranquility Base. Houston. You can start your powerdown now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. It's in progress.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And, Tranquility Base, the White Team is going off now and letting the Maroon Team take over. We appreciate the great show. It was a beautiful Job, you guys.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Couldn't of had better agreement from all of you back there.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Tranquility.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go, Tranquility. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Our recommendation at this point is planning an EVA with your concurrence starting about eight o'clock this evening, Houston time. That is about 3 hours from now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Well, we will give you some time to think about that.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. We thought about it; we will support it. You're GO at that time. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: You guys are getting prime time TV there.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Hope that little TV set works, but we'll see.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Tranquility Base. Houston. Was your eight o'clock Houston time a reference to opening the hatch or starting the PREP for EVA at that time? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: That would be hatch opening.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's what we thought. Thank you much.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: That might be a little later than that, but in other words, start the PREP in about an hour or so.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. Copy NOUN 49?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by, Columbia.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. That's fine. We are ready to support you any time, Neil. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Break. Columbia, we see the NOUN 49. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We got the data. We would like a VERB 34. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: All right. Stand by one, Charlie, for the next one.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Columbia. Did - How did Tranquility look to you down there? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Well, the area looks smooth, but I was unable to see him. I just picked out a distinguishable crater nearby and marked on it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: It looks like a nice area, though.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Columbia. Houston. I understand you could not see Tranquility. What were you marking on? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. I say again, I could not see him. AUTO optics pointed at a spot very close to the coordinates which you gave me, so I picked a tiny crater in that area and marked on it so I will be able to have repeatable data, but I was unable to see him.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Tranquility Base. Houston. On our DPS venting and that fuel problem, our heat exchanger is cleared up. We heard that the ice is melted, and we are in good shape now. Out.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston. Tranquility is going to put the track modes in P00 now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Columbia. Go.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We noticed you are maneuvering very close to gimbal lock. I suggest you move back away. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes. I am going around it, doing this CMC AUTO maneuvers to the PAD values of roll 270, pitch 101, yaw 45.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Columbia.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: How about sending me a fourth gimbal for Christmas.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. You were unreadable. Say again please.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Disregard.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Several items for you. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. First of all, we'd like a waste water dump to 10 percent on the backside. Secondly, it does not look like we are going to need any plane change at this time, so we will not be uplinking a new REFSMMAT. Third item, I would like all of your CRYO heaters to AUTO, and we are ready for a battery charge, battery BRAVO; it will last about 7 hours. If you should go to sleep, we will be terminating that BATT charge, but at the moment, we can go ahead and start the BATT charge on BATT Bravo. And a final item, for your SM RCS configuration for your rest period, register 1 for the DAP is 11111; DAP register 2, 01100. And your AUTO RCS select switches, quad Alfa, pitch jets on only, quad Bravo all on, quad Charlie and quad Delta all off. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Dump waste water to 10 percent on the backside. Use prior REFSMMAT, CRYO heaters on to AUTO, battery B charge until I go to sleep. DAP is 11111, 01100. Select quads A pitch only on, C and D all up. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We will have a state vector update for you a little later. We are not prepared with it right now; and on another subject, from Tranquility Base, they are prepared to begin their EVA early. They expect to begin DEPRESS operations in about 3 hours at 108, approximately 108 GET. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Sounds good to me. Tell them to eat some lunch before they go.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We'd like your PRD readouts when possible, and we've checked over your EM dump. It all looks okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, Houston. We'd like your PRD readout, and we have double checked your EM dump. It all looks okay. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Understand our E memory dump was good. CDR's dosimeter is 11014.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And LMP is 09011.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Tranquility. Break. Columbia, we would like for you to REACQ with your high gain; attempt a manual lock on. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Tranquility here. The LMP's readout may possibly be 09017. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, Houston. Roger. 09017 is an update on your readout.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Columbia's in high gain.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I'll let you know for sure when it goes to either 12 or 18.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, Houston. Roger. The medics report your latter reading, 17, appears to be the correct one. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Columbia's in the high gain.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Columbia. You're sounding much better now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbla, Houston. Request P00 in ACCEPT, and we'll uplink another state vector. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Going P00 in ACCEPT.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Suggest you put BATT A on your BATT relay bus. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We're through with your computer. You can go to BLOCK.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. BLOCK.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston. Tranquility Base.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. We've reviewed the checklist, and about the only change in order to advance the EVA that we've found is that you'll want to delay your lithium hydroxide change until after the EVA rather than before. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. We'd just as soon make a change and jettison the old one. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. We would like to delay that LOIO - LiOH change until after the EVA. There is a possibility you could jettison the canister when you jettison your PLSS. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: All right. We'll plan it that way. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Tranquility.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We show your EVAP OUT temperature running low. Request you go to manual temperature control and bring it up. You can check the procedures in ECS MAL 17. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. I have a P22 update for you.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Columbia. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. Your P22 AUTO - AUTO optics landmark ID on LM. T1, 106 plus 30 plus 31; T2, 106 plus 35 plus 41, 2 nautical miles south. Your TCA, 106 plus 37 plus 16. Shaft angle 357.9 and trunnion angle 44.3. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Houston. We have your LOS in 3 minutes. AOS will be 106 plus 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. 0h 09 25 29 LMP (TRANQ) Houston, Tranquility. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, Houston. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. This is the LM pilot. I'd like to take this opportunity to ask every person listening in, whoever and wherever they may be, to pause for a moment and contemplate the events of the past few hours and to give thanks in his or her own way. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Tranquility Base.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: That's about ready to fall off.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, it just doesn't look like it sunk in at all.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. We'd like some estimate of how far along you are with your eating and when you may be ready to start you EVA PREP. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: I think that we'll be ready to start EVA PREP in about a half an hour or so.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Tranquility.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Columbia. How do you read?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, Columbia. This is Houston.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, this is Tranquility Base. We are beginning our EVA PREP.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility Base, this is Houston, Roger. Copy. You're beginning EVA PREP. Break. Break. Columbia, Columbia, this is Houston. Reading you loud and clear. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You're loud and clear. The waste water dump is down to 10 percent. I have a question on the P22. Do you want me to do another P22, or is all that information just for my own use in tracking the LM for photographic purposes?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Columbia, this is Houston. We request that you perform another P22. We'd like you to let the AUTO optics take care of the tracking and devote your energies to trying to pick out the LM on the lunar surface. If you can find the LM, of course. We're looking for marks on it; but tracking of geographical features doesn't do us all that much good. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. I'll do it. And on the ECS system, the - Whatever the problem was, it seems to have gone away without any changing of J52 sensors or anything like that. My glycol evaporator outlet TEMP is up above 50 now, and it's quite comfortable in the cockpit; so we'll talk more about that one later.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Columbia. Did you shift into manual control, or did the problem resolve itself under AUTO control? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: The problem went away under AUTO. Oh 10 12 55 CC Roger. That's the best type. Out.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I did cycle out of AUTO into - I did cycle out of AUTO into MANUAL, back into AUTO.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Houston. Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility Base, Tranquility Base, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, this is Houston. We need a second set of PRD readings so that we may establish a rate. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: CDR is reading 11O14.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: LMP is reading 09017 and three quarters.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Tranquility, this is Houston. We copy your readings, Out.
